newsitem.title: USA: Fire breaks out at Louisiana chemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Fire breaks out at Louisiana chemical plant.

text.p: A fire broke out at a chemical plant across the Mississippi River from the historic French Quarter in suburban New Orleans Wednesday, injuring one person, officials said.
Shipping traffic along the river was halted briefly while firefighters battled the blaze at a Witco Corp. plant in Gretna, La. Flames shot 100 feet (30 metres) into the air, officials said.
"I think some fuel oil ignited that was being transferred, but we're not sure yet," said Lloyd Moon, a spokesman for the Greenwich, Connecticut-based chemical company.
A small building housing a compressor unit was burned but no production units were damaged at the plant, which produces detergent additives and lubrication oils.
The plant will be shut down for a couple of days while firefighters and company officials determine what sparked the blaze and complete an inspection of the facility, he said.
